trap_mechanism: Student's intuition: tides are caused primarily by the Sun. Correct answer: primarily by the Moon with smaller contribution from Sun.
distractor_strategy: Includes statement about Sun causing tides as wrong option; uses student's intuitive but incorrect answer

trap_mechanism: Multiple statements about tides - student knows some facts but misses the subtle error in one statement about tidal mechanics
distractor_strategy: Includes mostly correct statements with one subtly wrong detail; student confirms what they know and misses the error

trap_mechanism: Correct concept (ocean current) paired with wrong temperature classification or wrong region
distractor_strategy: Uses correct current name but pairs with incorrect property (wrong temperature, wrong region, wrong direction)

trap_mechanism: Both assertion and reason are individually correct but not causally related; student thinks they're connected
distractor_strategy: Provides two individually true statements that students assume must be related

trap_mechanism: Student's intuition: cold currents are always found in high latitudes. Trap: some cold currents exist in equatorial regions (upwelling zones)
distractor_strategy: Makes student's intuitive but wrong answer available as plausible option

trap_mechanism: Question compares ocean salinity across multiple basins - student uses one metric (evaporation) but ignores others (river discharge, precipitation)
distractor_strategy: Correct answer requires weighing multiple factors; student focuses on one factor they know well

trap_mechanism: Question about El Niño causes - student focuses on recent news (warming Pacific) and forgets to verify mechanism
distractor_strategy: Includes recent news event as distractor; primes student to choose news-related answer

trap_mechanism: Ocean acidification: student confuses cause (CO2) with effect (pH reduction) or the mechanisms involved
distractor_strategy: Reverses cause-effect relationships in wrong answer options

trap_mechanism: Correct marine ecosystem but wrong depth zone or wrong environmental condition
distractor_strategy: Uses correct ecosystem name but pairs with wrong depth/temperature zone

trap_mechanism: Thermohaline circulation: student knows individual facts (salinity, temperature, deep water) but misses how they link globally
distractor_strategy: Includes correct individual facts but wrong connection between them

trap_mechanism: IOD vs ENSO distinction: student confuses which ocean system (Pacific vs Indian) and which months matter
distractor_strategy: Uses correct concept name but wrong ocean basin or wrong seasonal pattern

trap_mechanism: Ocean zones by light penetration - student knows zone names but misses depth ranges or wrong organism distribution
distractor_strategy: Correct zone name with incorrect depth or light penetration characteristic
